summary: Iter 12 — Frontend-only verification of the GitHub-integration deliverables for La Clase Digital. Tested via Playwright using JWT minted directly with JWT_SECRET (HS256). 8/8 checks passed: Module 0 banner (mod-ia-00) renders with data-testid='module-banner-github-intro' and not the M5 banner; Module 5 banner (mod-ia-05) renders with data-testid='module-banner-github-pages' and not the M0 banner; Module 1 (mod-ia-01) shows neither banner. TaskDetail.jsx exposes the optional repo_url input (data-testid='task-submit-repo'), the existing pending submission for test.student renders the clickable link data-testid='task-submission-repo-92f61751-…' pointing to https://github.com/test-student/curso-ia-ele, and a brand-new submission posted via the form persists repo_url=https://github.com/test-student/iter12-test and re-renders it as a link in 'Mis entregas'. Admin /admin 'Entregas pendientes' shows BOTH the user's profile github_url (data-testid='admin-user-github-{id}', href=https://github.com/test-student) and the per-submission repo_url (data-testid='admin-submission-repo-{id}', href=https://github.com/test-student/curso-ia-ele) above the submission body, exactly as required. Backend POST /course/ia-ele/task/mod-ia-00-task/submit accepted {repo_url} → 200 and the value round-tripped through GET /course/ia-ele/task/{id} and GET /admin/overview.
critical_code_review_comments: Cosmetic only: TaskDetail.jsx submit() does not strip whitespace from repo_url input on the URL field but does .trim() before posting — fine. Consider adding client-side URL validation (regex github.com) before submit to give immediate feedback; today the server accepts any string in repo_url. Not blocking.

Admin.jsx inline anchor for downloading submission embeds token in href as ?t=… as a fallback before the onClick blob fetch — token-in-URL would leak via referrer if the user middle-clicked. The onClick preventDefault+blob path is the primary path so this is mitigated; consider removing the t= fallback href to avoid token leakage.

ModuleDetail.jsx hardcodes order===0 and order===5 for the two banners. If module ordering is reshuffled via the admin reorder endpoint, the banners follow `order` and could drift from the intended modules (mod-ia-00 / mod-ia-05). Safer would be matching on entry.module.id === 'mod-ia-00' / 'mod-ia-05'. Not blocking for current data.
